The toolbox reads external gridded data through HydroMT catalogs. The project names catalogs and source entries; the data files are not distributed with the workflow code. The [2025 CST technical note](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/docs/references/cst-toolbox-technical-note-2025.md) describes the recommended global datasets and their scientific roles. The table below adapts that inventory to the [current project template](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/templates/project_config.template.yml), [data catalog](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/catalogs/deltares_data.yml), and [projection template](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/templates/project_config.analyze_projections.template.yml). It is a source-role guide, not a claim that every listed source is enabled or locally available.

## Spatial data for the basin and model

| Data class and example source | Use in the toolbox | Assessment sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Hydrography and basin index — MERIT Hydro | Delineate the drainage area, establish flow directions and river cells, and place output points on the network | Basin extent, upstream area, routing, and location identity can change with the hydrography or snapping rules |
| River geometry — Lin et al. river data | Inform river width or related geometry in the model setup | Flow travel time and channel response can change |
| Land cover — VITO | Classify land surface and derive vegetation or surface parameters through HydroMT-Wflow mappings | Interception, evapotranspiration, infiltration, and runoff partitioning can change |
| Leaf area index — MODIS LAI | Describe vegetation seasonality in the model maps | Evapotranspiration and interception behavior can change |
| Soil properties — SoilGrids | Derive spatial soil and storage parameters | Soil-water storage, recharge, and low-flow response can change |
| Lakes and reservoirs — HydroLakes and configured inventories | Represent waterbodies where the model setup includes them | Storage and routed flows can change, especially in regulated basins |
| Glaciers — Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI), when configured | Define glacier areas for relevant basins | Snow and ice contributions to seasonal flow can change |

These products have different native spatial support, observation periods, and uncertainties. Resampling them to one Wflow grid does not make their information equally precise. The model grid resolution is therefore a computational choice, not a statement of the effective resolution of soil, land-cover, or river parameters. Review basin boundaries, drainage structure, elevation, land cover, and known waterbodies after setup, especially where a small spatial error could move an outlet or change upstream area.

## Historical meteorology and observations

| Source | Role | Checks before assessment |
|---|---|---|
| ERA5 daily forcing | Supplies the selected historical meteorology in the supplied example; drives the historical Wflow run and conditions weather generation | Coverage over the basin and time window, variable units, precipitation magnitude and seasonality, temperature, and missing values |
| CHIRPS precipitation | Alternative or candidate precipitation source for historical-climate comparison | Geographic coverage, rainfall seasonality and extremes, and consistency with the other forcing variables needed by the model and generator |
| Local observed time series | Optional evaluation at configured output locations | Gauge location and drainage area, overlap with the model period, units, missing days, and known regulation or abstraction |

The [2025 note](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/docs/references/cst-toolbox-technical-note-2025.md) identifies historical meteorology as serving **two purposes**: forcing the hydrological model and conditioning the stochastic weather generator. This makes source selection unusually consequential in the current toolbox, which does not locally calibrate the model. WF0 can compare available climate variables across candidate sources before one is selected. In the current pipeline, CHIRPS supplies precipitation; when it is selected, ERA5 contributes the other variables needed for model building and weather generation. A structurally complete climate store is not, by itself, a scientific validation of the forcing.

The historical extraction window must cover the historical model run and provide enough complete years for the weather generator. The project template requires at least 16 inclusive years. Compare source behavior with local stations or hydrological evidence where available; gridded products may smooth local extremes or miss topographic gradients even when basin-average statistics look plausible.

## Future climate information

WF2 reads configured **CMIP6** model, scenario, ensemble-member, reference-window, and future-window selections. It summarizes changes in precipitation and temperature for each combination. The results provide an overlay on the stress-test response surface, not forcing for WF3. Changing the CMIP6 ensemble or windows therefore changes the plausibility comparison, not an already generated scenario collection. Align its relative precipitation changes and absolute temperature changes with the stress-test axes before plotting them together.

The [projection settings template](https://github.com/tanerumit/blueearth_cst/blob/main/config/templates/project_config.analyze_projections.template.yml) shows example selections; it is not a prescribed ensemble for every basin. The number of available models and members, spatial resolution, and variable coverage depend on the catalog. Ensemble spread describes differences among those available projections, not a calibrated probability distribution for basin-scale outcomes.

## Choosing, replacing, and recording sources

HydroMT catalogs allow a project to name alternative data products without embedding file paths in the workflow. A substitute must still provide the variables, units, geometry, temporal coverage, and HydroMT-readable structure expected by the model setup. Changing a source can require rebuilding the model or regenerating the weather collection before results are comparable.

Record the catalog and entry names, source product and version, spatial resolution, temporal windows, any local preprocessing, and the observation series used for evaluation. Keep these with the run records when comparing basins or rerunning an assessment. For the exact configuration locations and path rules, see [Configuring a project](../guide/configuration.qmd).
